source.text: וְאֵ֛לֶּה אֲשֶׁר־נָחֲל֥וּ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בְּאֶ֣רֶץ כְּנָ֑עַן אֲשֶׁ֨ר נִֽחֲל֜וּ אוֹתָ֗ם אֶלְעָזָ֤ר הַכֹּהֵן֙ וִיהוֹשֻׁ֣עַ בִּן־נ֔וּן וְרָאשֵׁ֛י אֲב֥וֹת הַמַּטּ֖וֹת לִבְנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And these [are what] inherited [the] sons of Israel in [the] land of Canaan, which gave as inheritance them Eleazar the priest and Joshua son of Nun and [the] heads of [the] fathers of the tribes of [the] sons of Israel.

en.L: And these [are what] the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel inherited in the land of Canaan, which Eleazar the priest and Joshua son of Nun and the heads of the fathers of the tribes of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel gave them as an inheritance.
en.B: These are the lands that the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} received as their inheritance in the land of Canaan. Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun and the family heads of the tribes of Israel assigned these lands to them.
en.R: This is the land in Canaan that the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} received as their own. Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun and the family leaders of the tribes of Israel divided it among them.

sw.L: Na hizi [ndizo nchi] ambazo wana wa Israeli walirithi katika nchi ya Kanaani, ambazo Eleazari kuhani na Yoshua mwana wa Nuni na wakuu wa baba wa makabila ya wana wa Israeli waliwapa kuwa urithi.
sw.B: Hizi ndizo nchi ambazo Waisraeli walipokea kuwa urithi wao katika nchi ya Kanaani. Eleazari kuhani, Yoshua mwana wa Nuni na wakuu wa jamaa za makabila ya Israeli ndio waliowagawia nchi hizo.
sw.R: Hii ndiyo nchi ya Kanaani ambayo Waisraeli walipokea iwe yao. Eleazari kuhani, Yoshua mwana wa Nuni na viongozi wa jamaa za makabila ya Israeli waliigawa kati yao.

decisions.choice: these: points ahead to the lists that follow, through chapter 19
decisions.reason: "These" introduces the whole account of the land west of the Jordan given to the tribes, which runs from here to 19:51, where a closing line names the same three parties: Eleazar, Joshua and the heads of the families.

decisions.choice: inherited / gave as an inheritance: received, or handed out, land as a lasting family holding
decisions.reason: The same verb is used twice: first for the people who receive the land, then, in another form, for the leaders who give it out. An inheritance here is land held by a family from generation to generation, a gift from God that was not to be sold away for good (Leviticus 25:23; Numbers 36:7).

decisions.choice: Eleazar the priest and Joshua: the two men God appointed to divide the land
decisions.reason: God had named Eleazar and Joshua, with one leader from each tribe, to share out the land (Numbers 34:16-29). The priest stands first, as in Numbers 34:17, since the lot was cast before the LORD (18:6).

decisions.choice: the heads of the fathers: the heads of the ancestral families
decisions.reason: "Fathers" here is short for "houses of the fathers", the extended families that made up a tribe. Their heads were the leaders who acted for each tribe (Numbers 34:18; 36:1).

decisions.choice: the lands / the land
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "these [are what] they inherited". Balanced and Readable say what is meant: the land each tribe received.

source.text: בְּגוֹרַ֖ל נַחֲלָתָ֑ם כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר צִוָּ֤ה יְהוָה֙ בְּיַד־מֹשֶׁ֔ה לְתִשְׁעַ֥ת הַמַּטּ֖וֹת וַחֲצִ֥י הַמַּטֶּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: By [the] lot [was] their inheritance, as commanded Yahweh by [the] hand of Moses, for [the] nine tribes and [the] half of the tribe.

en.L: By the lot [was] their inheritance, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded by the hand of Moses, for the nine tribes and the half of the tribe.
en.B: Their inheritance was assigned by lot, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded through Moses, for the nine and a half tribes.
en.R: They used lots to decide which land each tribe would get, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded through Moses. This was done for the nine and a half tribes.

sw.L: Kwa kura [ulikuwa] urithi wao, kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alivyokuwa ameamuru kwa mkono wa Musa, kwa makabila tisa na nusu ya kabila.
sw.B: Urithi wao uligawiwa kwa kura, kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alivyokuwa ameamuru kupitia Musa, kwa makabila tisa na nusu.
sw.R: Walipiga kura ili kujua kila kabila lingepata nchi gani, kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alivyokuwa ameamuru kupitia Musa. Hivyo ndivyo walivyofanya kwa makabila tisa na nusu.

decisions.choice: by lot: the land was shared out by casting lots
decisions.reason: Lots were marked stones or sticks drawn or thrown to reach a decision. God had commanded that the land be divided this way (Numbers 26:55-56; 33:54; 34:13). The result was not left to chance or to the leaders' preference; it was taken as the LORD's own choice (Proverbs 16:33), and the lots were cast before him (18:6).

decisions.choice: by the hand of Moses: through Moses
decisions.reason: "By the hand of" someone means by means of him. God gave the command, and Moses passed it on.

decisions.choice: the nine tribes and the half of the tribe: the tribes still to receive land west of the Jordan
decisions.reason: The half tribe is the western half of Manasseh. The other two and a half tribes already had their land east of the Jordan (verse 3; 13:8).

decisions.choice: They used lots to decide which land each tribe would get
decisions.reason: Readable explains what "by lot" means, since many readers do not know the practice.

decisions.choice: the nine and a half tribes
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "the half of the tribe"; Balanced and Readable use the common English way of counting it.

source.text: כִּֽי־נָתַ֨ן מֹשֶׁ֜ה נַחֲלַ֨ת שְׁנֵ֤י הַמַּטּוֹת֙ וַחֲצִ֣י הַמַּטֶּ֔ה מֵעֵ֖בֶר לַיַּרְדֵּ֑ן וְלַ֨לְוִיִּ֔ם לֹֽא־נָתַ֥ן נַחֲלָ֖ה בְּתוֹכָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: For had given Moses [the] inheritance of [the] two tribes and [the] half of the tribe from beyond the Jordan, and to the Levites not he gave inheritance among them.

en.L: For Moses had given the inheritance of the two tribes and the half of the tribe across the Jordan; but to the Levites he did not give an inheritance among them.
en.B: Moses had already given the two and a half tribes their inheritance east of the Jordan, but he did not give the Levites an inheritance among the others.
en.R: Moses had already given land on the east side of the Jordan to two and a half tribes. But he did not give the Levites any land of their own among the other tribes.

sw.L: Kwa maana Musa alikuwa amewapa makabila mawili na nusu ya kabila urithi wao ng'ambo ya Yordani; lakini Walawi hakuwapa urithi kati yao.
sw.B: Musa alikuwa amekwisha kuwapa makabila mawili na nusu urithi wao upande wa mashariki wa Yordani, lakini hakuwapa Walawi urithi kati ya wengine.
sw.R: Musa alikuwa amekwisha kuwapa makabila mawili na nusu nchi upande wa mashariki wa Yordani. Lakini Walawi hakuwapa nchi yao wenyewe kati ya makabila mengine.

decisions.choice: across the Jordan: here the land east of the river
decisions.reason: The phrase means "on the other side of the Jordan", and the side depends on the speaker's viewpoint. The story now stands west of the river, so it names the land of Reuben, Gad and half of Manasseh to the east (13:8; Numbers 32:33).

decisions.choice: for Moses had given: explains why only nine and a half tribes are left
decisions.reason: "For" gives the reason for verse 2. The verb points back to what Moses had done before his death (Numbers 32; Joshua 13:8-32), so the share-out here concerns only the rest.

decisions.choice: no inheritance for the Levites: their share was the LORD himself
decisions.reason: The tribe of Levi received no tribal territory. Its share was the LORD and the offerings given to him (13:14, 33; Numbers 18:20-24; Deuteronomy 18:1-2). Verse 4 says what they did receive.

decisions.choice: east of the Jordan
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the side of the river, since "across the Jordan" alone does not say which side is meant.

source.text: כִּֽי־הָי֧וּ בְנֵֽי־יוֹסֵ֛ף שְׁנֵ֥י מַטּ֖וֹת מְנַשֶּׁ֣ה וְאֶפְרָ֑יִם וְלֹֽא־נָתְנוּ֩ חֵ֨לֶק לַלְוִיִּ֜ם בָּאָ֗רֶץ כִּ֤י אִם־עָרִים֙ לָשֶׁ֔בֶת וּמִ֨גְרְשֵׁיהֶ֔ם לְמִקְנֵיהֶ֖ם וּלְקִנְיָנָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: For were [the] sons of Joseph two tribes, Manasseh and Ephraim; and not they gave portion to the Levites in the land, except cities to dwell [in] and their pasture lands for their livestock and for their property.

en.L: For the {{gender:children|sons}} of Joseph were two tribes, Manasseh and Ephraim; and they did not give a portion to the Levites in the land, except cities to dwell [in] and their pasturelands for their livestock and for their property.
en.B: The descendants of Joseph had become two tribes, Manasseh and Ephraim. The Levites were given no share of the land, only towns to live in, with the pasturelands around them for their flocks and herds.
en.R: Joseph's descendants had become two tribes, Manasseh and Ephraim. So there were still twelve tribes to receive land. The Levites did not get any land of their own. They got only towns to live in, along with fields around the towns for their animals.

sw.L: Kwa maana wana wa Yusufu walikuwa makabila mawili, Manase na Efraimu; nao hawakuwapa Walawi fungu katika nchi, isipokuwa miji ya kukaa na malisho yake kwa ajili ya mifugo yao na kwa ajili ya mali yao.
sw.B: Wazao wa Yusufu walikuwa wamekuwa makabila mawili, Manase na Efraimu. Walawi hawakupewa fungu la nchi, ila miji ya kuishi tu, pamoja na malisho yaliyoizunguka kwa ajili ya makundi yao ya mifugo.
sw.R: Wazao wa Yusufu walikuwa wamekuwa makabila mawili, Manase na Efraimu. Kwa hiyo bado yalikuwa makabila kumi na mawili ya kupokea nchi. Walawi hawakupata nchi yao wenyewe. Walipata miji ya kuishi tu, pamoja na mashamba yaliyoizunguka kwa ajili ya wanyama wao.

decisions.choice: the sons of Joseph were two tribes: Joseph's line counted as two tribes
decisions.reason: Jacob adopted Joseph's two sons, Ephraim and Manasseh, as his own (Genesis 48:5), so each became a tribe. Leaving Levi out and counting Joseph twice keeps the number of tribes with land at twelve.

decisions.choice: for: gives the reason for the count of tribes in verses 2-3
decisions.reason: The first "for" explains how there can be nine and a half tribes in the west and two and a half in the east when Levi has no land: Joseph's descendants make two tribes.

decisions.choice: cities to dwell in, and their pasturelands: towns among the other tribes, with open land around them
decisions.reason: The Levites were given towns to live in scattered through the land, with a belt of open ground around each for grazing (Numbers 35:1-8). Chapter 21 lists the forty-eight towns.

decisions.choice: livestock and property: their animals and other goods
decisions.reason: The first word means livestock. The second means what someone has acquired, and here, beside pastureland, it chiefly means the animals that make up a person's wealth.

decisions.choice: The Levites were given ...; flocks and herds
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "they did not give" with no subject named; Balanced turns it into a passive. "Flocks and herds" gives the sense of the two words for animals and property.

decisions.choice: So there were still twelve tribes to receive land.
decisions.reason: Readable states the point that the verse makes by joining it to verses 2-3: with Joseph as two tribes, the number twelve is kept even without Levi.

source.text: כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר צִוָּ֤ה יְהוָה֙ אֶת־מֹשֶׁ֔ה כֵּ֥ן עָשׂ֖וּ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַֽיַּחְלְק֖וּ אֶת־הָאָֽרֶץ׃פ

records.literal_gloss: Just as commanded Yahweh Moses, so did [the] sons of Israel; and they divided the land.

en.L: Just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded Moses, so the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel did; and they divided the land.
en.B: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} did just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded Moses, and they divided up the land.
en.R: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} divided up the land. They did it just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded Moses.

sw.L: Kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alivyokuwa amemwamuru Musa, ndivyo wana wa Israeli walivyofanya; wakaigawa nchi.
sw.B: Waisraeli walifanya kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alivyokuwa amemwamuru Musa, wakaigawanya nchi.
sw.R: Waisraeli waliigawanya nchi. Walifanya sawasawa na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alivyokuwa amemwamuru Musa.

decisions.choice: as the LORD had commanded Moses: the commands of Numbers 26 and 34
decisions.reason: God had told Moses how the land was to be divided: by lot, by tribes, larger shares for larger tribes (Numbers 26:52-56; 33:54; 34:1-29). The people now carry out those orders.

decisions.choice: they divided the land: a summary of the share-out told in chapters 14-19
decisions.reason: The verse sums up the whole work that the next chapters describe tribe by tribe. It begins here with Judah and Caleb.

decisions.choice: The Israelites did just as ... / divided up the land. They did it just as ...
decisions.reason: The Hebrew puts "just as the LORD commanded" first for weight. Balanced and Readable put the people first, as English usually does.

source.text: וַיִּגְּשׁ֨וּ בְנֵֽי־יְהוּדָ֤ה אֶל־יְהוֹשֻׁ֨עַ֙ בַּגִּלְגָּ֔ל וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֔יו כָּלֵ֥ב בֶּן־יְפֻנֶּ֖ה הַקְּנִזִּ֑י אַתָּ֣ה יָדַ֡עְתָּ אֶֽת־הַדָּבָר֩ אֲשֶׁר־דִּבֶּ֨ר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֣ה אִישׁ־הָאֱלֹהִ֗ים עַ֧ל אֹדוֹתַ֛י וְעַ֥ל אֹדוֹתֶ֖יךָ בְּקָדֵ֥שׁ בַּרְנֵֽעַ׃

records.literal_gloss: And approached [the] sons of Judah to Joshua in Gilgal, and said to him Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite, You know the word that spoke Yahweh to Moses, [the] man of the God, concerning me and concerning you in Kadesh-barnea.

en.L: And the sons of Judah approached Joshua in Gilgal, and Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite said to him, "You know the word that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses the man of God concerning me and concerning you at Kadesh-barnea.
en.B: The men of Judah came to Joshua at Gilgal. Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite spoke to him: "You know what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} told Moses the man of God at Kadesh-barnea concerning you and me.
en.R: Some men from the tribe of Judah came to Joshua at Gilgal. One of them was Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite. He said to Joshua, "You know what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} told Moses, the man of God, about you and me at Kadesh-barnea.

sw.L: Na wana wa Yuda wakamkaribia Yoshua huko Gilgali, na Kalebu mwana wa Yefune Mkenizi akamwambia, "Wewe unajua neno ambalo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alimwambia Musa mtu wa Mungu kunihusu mimi na kukuhusu wewe huko Kadesh-barnea.
sw.B: Watu wa Yuda walimjia Yoshua huko Gilgali. Kalebu mwana wa Yefune, Mkenizi, akamwambia, "Unajua jambo ambalo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alimwambia Musa mtu wa Mungu huko Kadesh-barnea kuhusu wewe na mimi.
sw.R: Baadhi ya watu wa kabila la Yuda walimjia Yoshua huko Gilgali. Mmoja wao alikuwa Kalebu mwana wa Yefune, Mkenizi. Akamwambia Yoshua, "Unajua kile ambacho {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alimwambia Musa, mtu wa Mungu, kuhusu wewe na mimi huko Kadesh-barnea.

decisions.choice: the sons of Judah: members of the tribe of Judah who come with Caleb
decisions.reason: Caleb had stood for Judah among the twelve spies (Numbers 13:6), and Judah is the first tribe to receive land west of the Jordan (chapter 15). The men of his tribe come with him to Joshua, giving weight to his request.

decisions.choice: the Kenizzite: of the family of Kenaz
decisions.reason: Caleb is called a Kenizzite here and in verse 14, as in Numbers 32:12. Kenaz is a name found in Edom's family line (Genesis 36:11) and among the peoples of Canaan (Genesis 15:19), so his family may have come from outside and been joined to Judah. The text does not say more.

decisions.choice: the word the LORD spoke at Kadesh-barnea: the promise of Numbers 14
decisions.reason: When the people refused to enter the land, God said that of all that generation only Caleb and Joshua would enter it, and that Caleb would receive the land he had gone into (Numbers 14:24, 30; Deuteronomy 1:36). Caleb reminds Joshua of a promise that concerned them both.

decisions.choice: the man of God: a title for a prophet, one who speaks for God
decisions.reason: The title marks Moses as God's messenger (Deuteronomy 33:1). Caleb uses it because his claim rests on what God said through him.

decisions.choice: Gilgal: Israel's base camp near Jericho
decisions.reason: Israel had camped at Gilgal since crossing the Jordan (4:19; 5:9-10), and Joshua returned there after his campaigns (10:15, 43).

decisions.choice: the men of Judah / Some men from the tribe of Judah
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "sons of Judah" can mean the whole tribe, but here it is a group who come to Joshua with Caleb, so Balanced and Readable say "men". Readable adds "One of them" to show that Caleb is among them.

source.text: בֶּן־אַרְבָּעִ֨ים שָׁנָ֜ה אָנֹכִ֗י בִּ֠שְׁלֹחַ מֹשֶׁ֨ה עֶֽבֶד־יְהוָ֥ה אֹתִ֛י מִקָּדֵ֥שׁ בַּרְנֵ֖עַ לְרַגֵּ֣ל אֶת־הָאָ֑רֶץ וָאָשֵׁ֤ב אֹתוֹ֙ דָּבָ֔ר כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר עִם־לְבָבִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: A son of forty years [was] I when sent Moses, [the] slave of Yahweh, me from Kadesh-barnea to spy out the land; and I brought back him word as [it was] with my heart.

en.L: I [was] forty years old when Moses the slave of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} sent me from Kadesh-barnea to spy out the land, and I brought back word to him as [it was] in my heart.
en.B: When Moses the servant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} sent me out from Kadesh-barnea to explore the land, I was forty years old. I brought him back a report that was true to what was in my heart.
en.R: I was forty when Moses, the servant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, sent me out from Kadesh-barnea to explore the land. When I came back, I told him honestly what I believed.

sw.L: Mimi [nilikuwa] mwana wa miaka arobaini Musa mtumishi wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliponituma kutoka Kadesh-barnea kuipeleleza nchi, nami nikamletea habari kama [ilivyokuwa] moyoni mwangu.
sw.B: Musa mtumishi wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliponituma kutoka Kadesh-barnea kuipeleleza nchi, nilikuwa na umri wa miaka arobaini. Nilimletea habari iliyolingana na yale yaliyokuwa moyoni mwangu.
sw.R: Nilikuwa na umri wa miaka arobaini Musa, mtumishi wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, aliponituma kutoka Kadesh-barnea kuipeleleza nchi. Niliporudi, nilimweleza kwa uaminifu yale niliyoamini.

decisions.choice: a son of forty years: forty years old
decisions.reason: Hebrew gives a person's age as being "a son of" so many years. The same form returns in verse 10.

decisions.choice: sent me from Kadesh-barnea to spy out the land: the mission of Numbers 13
decisions.reason: Moses sent twelve men, one from each tribe, to explore Canaan, and they reported back at Kadesh (Numbers 13:1-26; 32:8).

decisions.choice: as it was with my heart: a report that said what I truly believed
decisions.reason: The heart is the seat of thought and will. Caleb gave a report true to his own conviction, that Israel could take the land with God's help (Numbers 13:30; 14:6-9), not one shaped by fear like the others' (verse 8).

decisions.choice: the servant of the LORD: Moses' title of honor
decisions.reason: As in 1:1, the word is the word for a slave, one owned by a master; said of Moses and God it is a title for the one God chose and who belonged to him.

decisions.choice: slave (Literal) / servant (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As in 1:1, Literal shows the hard sense of the word; Balanced and Readable say "servant", since the point is belonging to God and serving him.

decisions.choice: explore
decisions.reason: The verb means to go through a land on foot to find out about it. "Spy out" stays at Literal; "explore" is the plainer word.

source.text: וְאַחַי֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָל֣וּ עִמִּ֔י הִמְסִ֖יו אֶת־לֵ֣ב הָעָ֑ם וְאָנֹכִ֣י מִלֵּ֔אתִי אַחֲרֵ֖י יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: But my brothers who went up with me made melt the heart of the people, but I filled after Yahweh my God.

en.L: But my brothers who went up with me made the heart of the people melt, while I fully followed after {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} my God.
en.B: My companions who went up with me made the people lose heart, but I followed {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} my God with all my heart.
en.R: The other men who went with me made the people afraid. But I followed {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} my God with all my heart.

sw.L: Lakini ndugu zangu waliopanda pamoja nami waliifanya mioyo ya watu iyeyuke, ila mimi nilimfuata {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wangu kwa ukamilifu.
sw.B: Wenzangu tuliopanda pamoja waliwavunja watu moyo, lakini mimi nilimfuata {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wangu kwa moyo wangu wote.
sw.R: Wale watu wengine waliokwenda pamoja nami waliwatia watu hofu. Lakini mimi nilimfuata {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wangu kwa moyo wangu wote.

decisions.choice: my brothers: the other men sent with me
decisions.reason: "Brothers" means fellow Israelites, here the other spies, all but Joshua (Numbers 13:31-33; 14:36-38).

decisions.choice: made the heart of the people melt: took away the people's courage
decisions.reason: A melting heart is courage that gives way to fear (2:11; 5:1; 7:5). Moses used the same words of these spies (Deuteronomy 1:28).

decisions.choice: I filled after the LORD: I followed the LORD fully
decisions.reason: "To fill after" someone is to follow them completely, holding nothing back. God used these words of Caleb at Kadesh (Numbers 14:24), and they are repeated in verses 9 and 14.

decisions.choice: fully followed after (Literal) / followed ... with all my heart (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The phrase is rendered as in Numbers 14:24 and 32:12, so a reader can see that Caleb is quoting God's own words about him.

decisions.choice: My companions
decisions.reason: "Brothers" here means fellow spies, not family; Balanced says "companions", Readable "the other men".

decisions.choice: "nilimfuata kwa ukamilifu" (I followed fully)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "I filled after the LORD", meaning a whole-hearted following. Literal keeps the idea of fullness with "kwa ukamilifu"; Balanced and Readable say "kwa moyo wangu wote", as the English does. The same wording returns in verses 9 and 14.

source.text: וַיִּשָּׁבַ֣ע מֹשֶׁ֗ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַהוּא֮ לֵאמֹר֒ אִם־לֹ֗א הָאָ֨רֶץ֙ אֲשֶׁ֨ר דָּרְכָ֤ה רַגְלְךָ֙ בָּ֔הּ לְךָ֨ תִֽהְיֶ֧ה לְנַחֲלָ֛ה וּלְבָנֶ֖יךָ עַד־עוֹלָ֑ם כִּ֣י מִלֵּ֔אתָ אַחֲרֵ֖י יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And swore Moses on that day, saying, If not the land which trod your foot on it, to you it will be for inheritance and to your sons until forever, because you filled after Yahweh my God.

en.L: And Moses swore on that day, saying, 'Surely the land on which your foot has trodden will be an inheritance for you and for your {{gender:children|sons}} forever, because you have fully followed after {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} my God.'
en.B: On that day Moses swore an oath: 'The land where you have set foot will surely be an inheritance for you and your descendants for all time, because you have followed {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} my God with all your heart.'
en.R: That same day Moses made a promise with an oath. He said, 'The land you have walked on will belong to you and your descendants forever. It will be yours because you followed {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} my God with all your heart.'

sw.L: Na Musa akaapa siku ile, akisema, 'Hakika nchi ambayo mguu wako umeikanyaga itakuwa urithi wako na wa wana wako milele, kwa sababu umemfuata {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wangu kwa ukamilifu.'
sw.B: Siku ile Musa aliapa: 'Nchi uliyoikanyaga kwa mguu wako hakika itakuwa urithi wako na wa wazao wako daima, kwa sababu umemfuata {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wangu kwa moyo wako wote.'
sw.R: Siku ile ile Musa aliahidi kwa kiapo. Alisema, 'Nchi uliyotembea juu yake itakuwa yako na ya wazao wako milele. Itakuwa yako kwa sababu ulimfuata {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wangu kwa moyo wako wote.'

decisions.choice: if not: the form of an oath, meaning "surely"
decisions.reason: In a Hebrew oath, "if not ..." leaves unsaid a curse on the one who swears if the thing does not happen. It works as a strong "surely".

decisions.choice: the land on which your foot has trodden: the land Caleb walked through as a spy
decisions.reason: Caleb had gone as far as Hebron (Numbers 13:22). Moses retold God's promise in these words: Caleb "will see it, and to him I will give the land on which he has trodden" (Deuteronomy 1:36).

decisions.choice: the LORD my God: Moses' own words, as Caleb quotes them
decisions.reason: "My God" belongs to the oath Moses spoke, which Caleb quotes. Caleb says "the LORD my God" for himself in verse 8.

decisions.choice: to your sons forever: a holding for Caleb's family line
decisions.reason: An inheritance passed down the family. Caleb's descendants, including his daughter Achsah (15:16-19), hold the land after him.

decisions.choice: made a promise with an oath. He said, ...
decisions.reason: Readable explains "swore" and breaks the oath into two sentences, repeating "It will be yours" to tie the reason to the promise.

source.text: וְעַתָּ֗ה הִנֵּה֩ הֶחֱיָ֨ה יְהוָ֣ה׀אוֹתִי֮ כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֵּר֒ זֶה֩ אַרְבָּעִ֨ים וְחָמֵ֜שׁ שָׁנָ֗ה מֵ֠אָז דִּבֶּ֨ר יְהוָ֜ה אֶת־הַדָּבָ֤ר הַזֶּה֙ אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־הָלַ֥ךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בַּמִּדְבָּ֑ר וְעַתָּה֙ הִנֵּ֣ה אָנֹכִ֣י הַיּ֔וֹם בֶּן־חָמֵ֥שׁ וּשְׁמוֹנִ֖ים שָׁנָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And now, see, has kept alive Yahweh me as he spoke, these forty and five years from when spoke Yahweh this word to Moses, when walked Israel in the wilderness; and now, see, I [am] today a son of five and eighty years.

en.L: And now, see, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has kept me alive, just as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} spoke, these forty-five years since {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke this word to Moses, while Israel walked in the wilderness; and now, see, I [am] today eighty-five years old.
en.B: Now {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has kept me alive, just as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} promised, for these forty-five years since {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said this to Moses, while Israel journeyed in the wilderness. And here I am today, eighty-five years old.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has kept me alive, just as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} promised. It has been forty-five years since {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said this to Moses, back when Israel was traveling in the desert. And look at me now! I am eighty-five years old today.

sw.L: Na sasa, tazama, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ameniweka hai, kama alivyosema, miaka hii arobaini na mitano tangu {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alipomwambia Musa neno hili, Israeli walipokuwa wakitembea nyikani; na sasa, tazama, mimi leo [ni] mwana wa miaka themanini na mitano.
sw.B: Sasa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ameniweka hai, kama alivyoahidi, kwa miaka hii arobaini na mitano tangu alipomwambia Musa jambo hilo, Israeli walipokuwa wakisafiri nyikani. Na mimi hapa leo, nina umri wa miaka themanini na mitano.
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ameniweka hai, kama alivyoahidi. Imepita miaka arobaini na mitano tangu alipomwambia Musa jambo hilo, wakati Israeli walipokuwa wakisafiri jangwani. Na sasa nitazame! Leo nina umri wa miaka themanini na mitano.

decisions.choice: as he spoke: as he promised
decisions.reason: God's word at Kadesh was a promise that Caleb would live to enter the land (Numbers 14:24, 30, 38). His being alive is the proof that God kept it.

decisions.choice: forty-five years: from Kadesh to the dividing of the land
decisions.reason: Caleb was forty at Kadesh and is now eighty-five. Israel spent thirty-eight years in the wilderness after leaving Kadesh (Deuteronomy 2:14), so these numbers imply that the wars of chapters 6-12 lasted about seven years.

decisions.choice: see: a word that calls the hearer to look at what is said
decisions.reason: Caleb uses it twice: first to point to God's care, then to himself standing there in old age.

decisions.choice: here I am / look at me now
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable express the second "see" in the way English points to oneself, and leave out the first, which "now" carries.

source.text: עוֹדֶ֨נִּי הַיּ֜וֹם חָזָ֗ק כַּֽאֲשֶׁר֙ בְּי֨וֹם שְׁלֹ֤חַ אוֹתִי֙ מֹשֶׁ֔ה כְּכֹ֥חִי אָ֖ז וּכְכֹ֣חִי עָ֑תָּה לַמִּלְחָמָ֖ה וְלָצֵ֥את וְלָבֽוֹא׃

records.literal_gloss: Still I [am] today strong as on [the] day sent me Moses; as my strength then and as my strength now, for war and to go out and to come in.

en.L: I [am] still strong today, as on the day Moses sent me; as my strength [was] then, so my strength [is] now, for war and for going out and for coming in.
en.B: Today I am just as strong as on the day Moses sent me. My strength now is what it was then, for war and for going out and coming in.
en.R: Today I am as strong as I was on the day Moses sent me out. I can still lead men out to battle and bring them home again, just as I could then.

sw.L: Bado [mimi] leo ni hodari kama siku ile Musa aliponituma; kama nguvu zangu [zilivyokuwa] wakati ule, ndivyo nguvu zangu [zilivyo] sasa, kwa vita na kwa kutoka na kwa kuingia.
sw.B: Leo bado nina nguvu kama siku ile Musa aliponituma. Nguvu zangu sasa ni kama zilivyokuwa wakati ule, kwa vita na kwa kutoka na kuingia.
sw.R: Leo nina nguvu kama nilivyokuwa siku ile Musa aliponituma. Bado ninaweza kuwaongoza watu kwenda vitani na kuwarudisha nyumbani, kama nilivyoweza wakati ule.

decisions.choice: going out and coming in: leading and taking part in all one's work, here especially in war
alternatives: the ordinary business of daily life
decisions.reason: The pair names the whole range of a person's activity, and is often used of a leader taking his people out to battle and back (Numbers 27:17; 1 Samuel 18:13, 16). Moses had said at a hundred and twenty that he could no longer go out and come in (Deuteronomy 31:2); Caleb, at eighty-five, says he still can.

decisions.choice: as my strength then, so my strength now: my strength has not changed
decisions.reason: The two "as" phrases set then and now side by side as equal.

decisions.choice: lead men out to battle and bring them home again
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom by the sense it has beside "for war". The phrase can be wider than leading in battle, so this is marked for reviewers.

source.text: וְעַתָּ֗ה תְּנָה־לִּי֙ אֶת־הָהָ֣ר הַזֶּ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־דִּבֶּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא כִּ֣י אַתָּֽה־שָׁמַעְתָּ֩ בַיּ֨וֹם הַה֜וּא כִּֽי־עֲנָקִ֣ים שָׁ֗ם וְעָרִים֙ גְּדֹל֣וֹת בְּצֻר֔וֹת אוּלַ֨י יְהוָ֤ה אוֹתִי֙ וְה֣וֹרַשְׁתִּ֔ים כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר דִּבֶּ֥ר יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And now give to me this hill country which spoke Yahweh on that day, for you heard on that day that Anakim [were] there and cities great, fortified. Perhaps Yahweh [will be] with me, and I will dispossess them as spoke Yahweh.

en.L: And now give me this hill country of which {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke on that day, for you heard on that day that Anakim [were] there, and cities great [and] fortified. Perhaps {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [will be] with me, and I will dispossess them, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke."
en.B: So now give me this hill country, the one {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} promised me on that day. You yourself heard then that the Anakim were there, with large fortified cities. Perhaps {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will be with me, and I will drive them out, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said."
en.R: So now give me this hill country that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} promised me that day. You heard then that the Anakim lived there. They were a people known for being very tall, and their cities were large and had strong walls. Perhaps {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will be with me. Then I will drive them out, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said."

sw.L: Na sasa nipe nchi hii ya milima ambayo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliisema siku ile, kwa maana wewe ulisikia siku ile kwamba Waanaki [walikuwa] huko, na miji mikubwa [yenye] ngome. Huenda {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} [atakuwa] pamoja nami, nami nitawafukuza, kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alivyosema."
sw.B: Basi sasa nipe nchi hii ya milima ambayo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliniahidi siku ile. Wewe mwenyewe ulisikia wakati ule kwamba Waanaki walikuwa huko, wakiwa na miji mikubwa yenye ngome. Huenda {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} atakuwa pamoja nami, nami nitawafukuza, kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alivyosema."
sw.R: Basi sasa nipe nchi hii ya milima ambayo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliniahidi siku ile. Ulisikia wakati ule kwamba Waanaki waliishi huko. Hao walikuwa watu waliojulikana kwa kuwa warefu sana, na miji yao ilikuwa mikubwa yenye kuta imara. Huenda {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} atakuwa pamoja nami. Ndipo nitawafukuza, kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alivyosema."

decisions.choice: this hill country: the hills around Hebron in the land of Judah
decisions.reason: "This" points to the region Caleb is asking for and that God spoke of, the hill country where Hebron stands (verse 13; Numbers 13:17, 22). Caleb names it as a place both men know.

decisions.choice: Anakim: a people of great size living around Hebron
decisions.reason: The descendants of Anak had frightened the spies (Numbers 13:22, 28, 33; Deuteronomy 9:2). Joshua had already fought them in the hill country (11:21-22), but some remained, and 15:13-14 tells how Caleb drove out the three clans of Anak from Hebron.

decisions.choice: perhaps the LORD will be with me: humble hope, not doubt of the promise
decisions.reason: Caleb does not doubt God's word, which he quotes at the end of the verse. "Perhaps" shows that he does not take God's help for granted: victory depends on the LORD being with him, not on his own strength (compare 1 Samuel 14:6).

decisions.choice: dispossess them: drive them out and take their land
decisions.reason: The verb means to take possession by driving out those who hold it.

decisions.choice: promised me
decisions.reason: "Spoke" here is the promise to Caleb in Numbers 14:24, so Balanced and Readable say "promised me".

decisions.choice: They were a people known for being very tall
decisions.reason: Readable says who the Anakim were, as Numbers 13:22 does, so that the reader sees why the request is bold.

source.text: וַֽיְבָרְכֵ֖הוּ יְהוֹשֻׁ֑עַ וַיִּתֵּ֧ן אֶת־חֶבְר֛וֹן לְכָלֵ֥ב בֶּן־יְפֻנֶּ֖ה לְנַחֲלָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And blessed him Joshua, and he gave Hebron to Caleb son of Jephunneh for inheritance.

en.L: And Joshua blessed him, and he gave Hebron to Caleb son of Jephunneh as an inheritance.
en.B: Joshua blessed him and gave Hebron to Caleb son of Jephunneh as his inheritance.
en.R: Joshua blessed Caleb and gave him the city of Hebron as his own land.

sw.L: Na Yoshua akambariki, akampa Kalebu mwana wa Yefune Hebroni kuwa urithi.
sw.B: Yoshua alimbariki, akampa Kalebu mwana wa Yefune Hebroni kuwa urithi wake.
sw.R: Yoshua alimbariki Kalebu, akampa mji wa Hebroni uwe nchi yake mwenyewe.

decisions.choice: blessed him: asked God's good on him and granted his request
decisions.reason: To bless someone here is to speak words that call down God's favor on him. Joshua's blessing goes with his approval of Caleb's claim, as Joshua later blesses the eastern tribes when he sends them home (22:6-7).

decisions.choice: Hebron: an ancient city in the hills of Judah
decisions.reason: Hebron was where Abraham had lived and where he bought the cave of Machpelah to bury Sarah (Genesis 13:18; 23:2, 19). It was the place the spies had reached (Numbers 13:22).

decisions.choice: Joshua blessed Caleb ... gave him the city of Hebron
decisions.reason: Readable names Caleb at once and adds "the city of" so the reader knows what Hebron is.

source.text: עַל־כֵּ֣ן הָיְתָֽה־חֶ֠בְרוֹן לְכָלֵ֨ב בֶּן־יְפֻנֶּ֤ה הַקְּנִזִּי֙ לְֽנַחֲלָ֔ה עַ֖ד הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה יַ֚עַן אֲשֶׁ֣ר מִלֵּ֔א אַחֲרֵ֕י יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: Therefore became Hebron Caleb's, son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite, for inheritance until this day, because that he filled after Yahweh, God of Israel.

en.L: Therefore Hebron became the inheritance of Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite until this day, because he fully followed after {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel.
en.B: So Hebron has belonged to Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite as his inheritance to this day, because he followed {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, with all his heart.
en.R: That is why Hebron still belongs to the family of Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite. It is theirs because Caleb followed {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, with all his heart.

sw.L: Kwa hiyo Hebroni ikawa urithi wa Kalebu mwana wa Yefune Mkenizi hadi siku hii ya leo, kwa sababu alimfuata {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wa Israeli, kwa ukamilifu.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo Hebroni imekuwa mali ya Kalebu mwana wa Yefune Mkenizi kuwa urithi wake hadi leo, kwa sababu alimfuata {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wa Israeli, kwa moyo wake wote.
sw.R: Ndiyo sababu Hebroni bado ni mali ya jamaa ya Kalebu mwana wa Yefune Mkenizi. Ni yao kwa sababu Kalebu alimfuata {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wa Israeli, kwa moyo wake wote.

decisions.choice: until this day: up to the writer's own time
decisions.reason: As in 5:9, "until this day" looks from the time the account was written back to the event, and says that Caleb's family still held Hebron then.

decisions.choice: because he followed the LORD fully: the reason for the gift, said a third time
decisions.reason: Caleb said it of himself (verse 8), Moses said it in his oath (verse 9), and the narrator now says it as the reason Caleb's family holds Hebron. The land came as a reward for loyal trust, as God had promised (Numbers 14:24).

decisions.choice: Hebron as Caleb's: the city's fields and villages
decisions.reason: Later Hebron was also made a city of refuge and a town for the priests, while its fields and villages stayed with Caleb (20:7; 21:11-12).

decisions.choice: fully followed after / followed ... with all his heart
decisions.reason: As in verse 8 and Numbers 14:24.

decisions.choice: the family of Caleb
decisions.reason: Readable says "the family of" because "until this day" means long after Caleb himself.

source.text: וְשֵׁ֨ם חֶבְר֤וֹן לְפָנִים֙ קִרְיַ֣ת אַרְבַּ֔ע הָאָדָ֧ם הַגָּד֛וֹל בָּעֲנָקִ֖ים ה֑וּא וְהָאָ֥רֶץ שָׁקְטָ֖ה מִמִּלְחָמָֽה׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And [the] name of Hebron before [was] Kiriath-arba; the man the great among the Anakim [was] he. And the land was quiet from war.

en.L: And the name of Hebron formerly [was] Kiriath-arba; he [was] the greatest man among the Anakim. And the land was quiet from war.
en.B: Hebron used to be called Kiriath-arba, after Arba, who was the greatest man among the Anakim. Then the land had peace from war.
en.R: Hebron was once called Kiriath-arba, which means the town of Arba. Arba had been the greatest of the Anakim. Then the land had peace, and the fighting stopped.

sw.L: Na jina la Hebroni zamani [lilikuwa] Kiriath-arba; yeye [alikuwa] mtu mkuu kuliko wote kati ya Waanaki. Na nchi ikastarehe bila vita.
sw.B: Hebroni zamani iliitwa Kiriath-arba, kwa jina la Arba, aliyekuwa mtu mkuu kuliko wote kati ya Waanaki. Kisha nchi ikawa na amani bila vita.
sw.R: Zamani Hebroni iliitwa Kiriath-arba, maana yake mji wa Arba. Arba alikuwa mkuu kuliko Waanaki wote. Kisha nchi ikawa na amani, na mapigano yakakoma.

decisions.choice: Kiriath-arba: "the town of Arba"
decisions.reason: "Kiriath" means town. The name could also be read "town of four", but the next words and 15:13 take Arba as a man, the father of Anak (also 21:11; Genesis 23:2).

decisions.choice: he: Arba, the man named in the old name of the city
decisions.reason: The pronoun has no other name near it to refer to, so it points to Arba in "Kiriath-arba".

decisions.choice: the land was quiet from war: the main fighting was over
decisions.reason: The same words close the account of the conquest in 11:23. Land still had to be taken (13:1-6), but there were no more great campaigns. Caleb's own fight for Hebron follows in 15:13-19.

decisions.choice: after Arba, who was
decisions.reason: Balanced names Arba so that "he" is clear; Readable explains the name.

decisions.choice: had peace
decisions.reason: As in 11:23 and for the same phrase in Judges, Literal says "was quiet" and the other levels say "had peace".

decisions.choice: "nchi ikastarehe" (Literal); "nchi ikawa na amani" (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The wording fixed for Joshua and Judges in the terms note: "the land was quiet" at Literal, "the land had peace" at Balanced and Readable.
